touches.text: Code that is no longer needed is deleted. Git history keeps it if we ever need it back. [Q#99: A retired path must not be named anywhere in the repo (the retirement proof, bin/proofs/test_retired_components_are_gone.py), except in records of truth: history, state, validations, verdicts. Measured 2026-11-13: a tester proof's measured fixture (ticket c8e421aac06e) lists a historical berth's writes_to, which holds skills/ruled/intention+why.json, and the retirement tooth reads that as a caller. Does a measured fixture count as a record that names what passed through, or must the fixture stop carrying the literal path?]

Lifetimes. Each tree declares its lifetime when it is made: kept, one activity (eg one sleep run), or until its source file changes. Dropping a tree drops its leaves and its own links. A node goes only when no tree indexes it, so whatever a temporary tree's activity promoted into a permanent tree outlives it. The drop is enforced, not a habit. WHY: a run that ends without dropping its tables leaves them behind forever.

Prebuild face: the chart chain, eight machines, each answering one question before a build begins: orient (what is asked, where does it live), constrain (what bounds it), survey (what already exists), decompose (how does it split), triage (what first, by what standard), hypothesize (what do we expect, how would we know we're wrong), validate (what does DONE mean, measured), and after the build, verdict (what done actually meant).
Hollow runs: proves a proof goes red when the build is removed.

A tooth whose live subject was deleted retires with it, when fixture teeth still cover the behaviour. Akien 2026-11-12, answering Q#87 (ce92eb562cf9 clause 6 read 6890cf7e4053's clause-2 tooth, deleted with the inference_calls table by 98ab0e9db57f): "i am good with retiring that".

The chart chain machines (9.3.2): orient, constrain, survey, decompose, triage, hypothesize, validate, verdict. [Q#98: The verdict's instrument run, and the proofs that exercise it, need bubblewrap, which Windows does not have, so `cairn test --exec` refuses there ("the instance seal is not confirmed ... bubblewrap (bwrap) is not installed") and three teeth stay red on Windows: test_the_instrument_is_run (two teeth) and the standing-verdict-proofs-stay-green check. Measured 2026-11-13. Whether Windows gets its own seal is the per-OS seal question in Q#90 (9.4.2.3.3); this one is the narrow choice that stands beside it: until that is settled, do the bwrap teeth skip on Windows (and read as not-run there), or do they stay red until Windows has a seal of its own?]
